title: Hybrid Mentorship & Skill-Pathways Playbook
author: Sana Patel
content:
Overview

Purpose
This playbook defines Redwood’s hybrid mentorship program and the companion skill-pathway framework. It is intended for new joiners, managers, mentors, and people-ops partners who are coordinating development journeys across remote and in-office rhythms. It explains eligibility, matching, time commitments, deliverables, tooling, and measurement.

Scope
- Applicable to all full-time employees and long-term contractors (>= 6 months).
- Covers: onboarding mentorship (first 90 days), role-based growth pathways, cross-functional stretch mentorships, and cohort learning events.
- Does not replace manager 1:1s, performance reviews, or external training budgets — it complements them.

Principles
- Intentionality: every mentorship pairing has a documented objective and time-bound plan.
- Hybrid-first: structure accommodates asynchronous work plus regular synchronous checkpoints.
- Portfolio mindset: employees maintain a short skill portfolio that maps to role expectations and stretch goals.
- Measurable outcomes: success is tracked with concrete milestones, not vague promises.

Program types
1) Onboarding Mentorship (0–90 days)
   - Goal: accelerate contributor impact and systems knowledge.
   - Duration: 12 weeks. Time commitment: mentor 2 hours/week average, mentee 3 hours/week including prep.
   - Deliverables: 90-day checklist signed off in the onboarding workspace, a 'first-features' shadow session, and a handover doc for the manager.

2) Role Growth Pathways (ongoing career ladders)
   - Goal: transparent competency development aligned with ladder expectations.
   - Duration: rolling; typical pathway 6–12 months.
   - Structure: skill modules (core role, adjacent skills, leadership craft) with checkpoints every quarter.

3) Stretch/Cross-Functional Mentorship (3–6 months)
   - Goal: enable discipline-crossing moves (e.g., SRE skills for a platform engineer).
   - Deliverables: capstone artifact (mini-project or case study) and a public writeup for knowledge sharing.

4) Mentorship Cohorts (1–2 months intensives)
   - Goal: focused learning (e.g., production-grade observability, interview calibration).
   - Format: weekly 90-minute sessions, group assignments, Slack cohort channel.

Roles & Responsibilities
- People Ops (program owner): program calendar, platform integrations (LMS / Notion / Slack), reporting, mentor training, quarterly retros.
- Manager: nominates mentee objectives, supports time allocation, approves development budget for external courses.
- Mentor: prepares a development plan, meets regularly, provides feedback and a final assessment.
- Mentee: owns the skill-portfolio, prepares for sessions, completes agreed artifacts.

Mentor Selection & Matching Process
1. Nomination & Self-Selection
   - Managers or individuals nominate mentors via the Mentorship Hub form (link in Tools section).
2. Automated Match + Human Review
   - People Ops runs the match algorithm weekly (skill-tag overlap, availability, past pairings). Matches are proposed to both parties for acceptance within 7 days.
3. Kickoff
   - Use the Kickoff Template to capture objectives, frequency, preferred regular slots, and success criteria. Both parties sign the kickoff doc in the Mentorship Hub.

Kickoff Template (required fields)
- Mentee name / role / manager
- Mentor name / discipline
- Start / end date
- Meeting cadence and preferred times
- Top 3 learning objectives (SMART)
- Deliverables / milestones
- Communication norms (async channels, response SLAs)
- Confidential items (if any)

Quarterly Cadence & Checkpoints
- Week 0 (kickoff): align objectives and logistics.
- Week 4: quick pulse — mentor submits a 1-paragraph progress note.
- Week 8: midpoint review — revisit objectives and adjust.
- Week 12: final review and a short public writeup of outcomes (unless confidential).
- For long-running pathways, checkpoints every 12 weeks.

Skill-Portfolio: structure and sample
- Purpose: a concise artifact (1–3 pages) the mentee maintains that maps skills to evidence and next steps.

Sample portfolio sections (plain text table)
- Skill | Level | Evidence | Next Steps\- Core backend fundamentals | Developing | PR reviews, observability ticket | Complete server tracing lab\- System design | Competent | Design doc for payments v2 | Pair with senior for architecture review

Tools & Integrations
- Mentorship Hub (Notion): central signup, kickoff & signoff templates, public case studies.
- Slack: #mentorship-cohort (announcements), private pair channels for ongoing communication.
- Learning Management System (LMS): course enrollments, recommended modules, and certifications.
- HRIS (Workday): used for eligibility verification and time-off coordination.
- Career Framework (internal): competency ladders and sample artifacts for each IC band.

Time & Budget Guidelines
- People Ops recommends 2–4 hours/week combined mentor+mentee for onboarding; 1–3 hours/week for ongoing mentorships.
- Development stipend: managers can allocate up to $1,500/year per head for paid courses related to approved pathways (manager approval required).
- Time taken for mentorship counts toward async development time; managers should protect this time in calendars.

Measurement & Success Criteria
- Inputs tracked: number of active mentorships, average session frequency, mentor acceptance rate, and program churn.
- Outcomes tracked: percent of mentees advancing skill levels on the career framework, self-reported confidence (pre/post survey), and manager-reported impact on OKRs.
- Targets (FY26): 70% of new hires assigned an onboarding mentor within 7 days, average session frequency >=1/week during first 6 weeks, and 30% of participants show measurable skill advancement within 6 months.

Mentor Training & Quality Assurance
- Mentor onboarding: 90-minute asynchronous course + a live quarterly workshop covering feedback best practices, psychological safety, and hybrid facilitation techniques.
- Calibration: People Ops facilitates a quarterly mentor forum to discuss hard cases and share materials.
- Complaints & Remediation: If a pairing is not working, escalate to people-ops@redwood.com who will propose a new match within 10 business days.

Manager playbook for supporting mentorships
1. Approve time: allocate recurring 1–2 hours/week for mentee development in calendars.
2. Align on goals: review the mentee’s portfolio and the mentorship kickoff doc within 2 weeks.
3. Re-assess at 12 weeks: sign off on final outcomes and decide next steps (extend, change focus, or close).

Confidentiality & Sensitive Topics
- Mentorship conversations are ordinarily private. If a topic involves HR or legal issues, the mentor should encourage the mentee to engage people-ops or HR.
- Certain artifacts (customer-sensitive designs, legal docs) should be marked as confidential and excluded from public writeups.

Sample FAQ
Q: Can I have multiple mentors?
A: Yes. A typical contributor will have an onboarding mentor and one or two ongoing mentors for specific skills.
Q: How long before I can be a mentor?
A: Active contributors with 12+ months at Redwood and positive peer feedback are eligible; exceptions considered by People Ops.
Q: What if my manager is my mentor?
A: Managers can mentor, but we recommend separate development mentors for candid career conversations.

Appendix: Quick templates and CLI snippets

- Slack command to register a session: /mentor register @mentor @mentee 2026-03-10 10:00PT
- Example milestone checklist (plain list):

  - [ ] Shadowed first workflow
  - [ ] Built artifact / demo
  - [ ] 12-week writeup uploaded
